A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CHTs/CHTss research. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–F in v1 and A–M in v2 support a reliable comparison despite substantial revision and retitling.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-classification, translation, language-modeling, zero-shot, runtime, and initialization-ablation results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 2, 4–5.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds CIFAR10 experiments, additional LLaMA sizes, FP32 comparisons, and extensive component and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: V2 introduces Bipartite Receptive Field initialization, replacing BSW initialization in the Transformer experiments. BRF uses distance-dependent connectivity and configurable fixed or uniform output-degree distributions, substantially changing the initialization procedure (Section 3.2 and Appendix D).

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR10 natural-color-image classification while retaining the MNIST-family datasets, three translation datasets, OpenWebText, and the existing zero-shot tasks. The additional LLaMA sizes expand model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds CHT to the corresponding translation and LLaMA-130M comparisons and CHTs to the zero-shot comparison. It removes the CHTs(GMP) result rows from Tables 2–3. Table 13 additionally compares removal criteria including SNIP and sensitivity-based rules.

E3.justification: New protocols include LLaMA-60M and 1B configurations, FP32 evaluation, ITOP tracking, and BRF parameter searches with best-setting selection. Table 7 reports a 130M FC learning rate of 1e-3 versus v1's unqualified 3e-3; this does not establish a rerun. Appendix H specifies a softness endpoint of 0.9, conflicting with the retained 0.75 in the main text.

E4.justification: V2 adds soft/random/deterministic regrowth analysis using ITOP, BRF initialization and degree-distribution sensitivity tests, Transformer component ablations, removal-rule and temperature comparisons, and FP32 robustness checks (Figure 3, Figures 7–12, Tables 9–13). Earlier BSW and BSF analyses are retained within Figures 6 and 8.

E5.justification: V2 identifies the retained MLP uncertainties as standard errors over three seeds and labels zero-shot uncertainties as standard deviations over five seeds. New translation plots specify standard errors over two or three seeds. V1's paired two-sided Wilcoxon test and p=0.01 statement are removed. These disclosures do not establish increased run counts.

E6.justification: The original MNIST-family values remain in Table 8, but v2 adds numerous results and revises retained CHTs/CHTss entries. CHTss's reported Multi30k BLEU at 95% sparsity changes from 32.04 to 32.82, while its 130M zero-shot average changes from 52.38 to 49.64. Revised initialization and settings prevent treating these as clean same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical BRF scoring and distance definitions and a stepwise complexity derivation for the node-based predictor (Appendices D and K). It also revises the sigmoid equation and removes the separate CH3-L3n definition; the existing integral argument is relocated to Appendix I. BRF Equation 7's distance weighting conflicts with the accompanying claim that nearby connections receive higher scores.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add BRF as a central contribution, including a claim of being the first brain-inspired network model for sparse initialization. V2 also extends the headline zero-shot superiority claim from CHTss alone to both CHTs and CHTss.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of BRF's spatial locality and degree control, and interprets task-dependent temperature preferences through the speed of weight learning. It uses the FP32 experiments to argue for greater reduced-precision robustness and practical suitability. The existing limitation concerning unavailable widespread sparse-training hardware remains.

D1.justification: V2 supplies predictor pseudocode, historical-weight restoration details, GPU models and counts, additional optimizer settings, and explanations of iterative warmup (Algorithm 1, Appendices J–M, Tables 5–7). Historical-weight reuse is newly documented; v1 does not specify regrown-weight initialization, so an underlying procedural change cannot be established from that disclosure alone.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted citations on synaptic plasticity, distance-dependent brain connectivity, ITOP, reduced precision, and removal criteria. BRF is explicitly positioned against ER, BSW, and BSF initialization. The existing DST and Cannistraci-Hebb related-work framework is largely retained.

P1.justification: The method exposition is substantially reorganized: path-based predictor material moves to Appendix C, density-decay derivations to Appendix I, and ablation discussion to Appendix H. Section 3.2 is rewritten around BRF, explanatory passages expand, and the title, author list, abstract, and conclusion are revised.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to predominantly one column. Figure 1's initialization schematic is revised, the topology illustration gains BRF panels, and numerous plots, heatmaps, tables, and a pseudocode display are added. The original MLP table moves to Table 8, while the language-model and zero-shot tables gain substantial structure.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation through direct CHT comparisons beyond MLPs, component ablations, an FP32 control for v1's precision explanation, and LLaMA-1B experiments previously left as future work. Pseudocode and implementation disclosures also improve assessability. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, although conflicting softness endpoints, the BRF formula/prose mismatch, and inconsistent 1B CHTss perplexities (15.41 in Table 3 versus 15.15 in Table 14) limit reproducibility.
